events.summary: Sports Ministry plans to take over and develop the Jayathilaka Sports Complex.
Nearly Rs. 4 million was allocated for urgent improvements at the complex.
Parliament spent Rs. 894 million on food and uniforms during 2020–2024.
Fifty homes for landslide-displaced families are scheduled to be handed over.
NHSL and KDU signed an agreement to provide cardiac surgery and specialist care.
Cabinet approved establishing a national centre to facilitate domestic business investment.
Cabinet approved awarding counter 10 operation to Casons Travel for three years.
Revised wastewater project cost rose from LKR 464 million to LKR 1.4 billion.
Officials said JICA funding of LKR 2 billion had been obtained to continue the project.
Groundbreaking marked the start of a Vavuniya University hostel under the 55-hostel project.
Former Speaker’s fuel expenditure was reported for 2023.
Ditwah-damaged Kotagala–Radella rail repairs were about 60% complete but slowed by bad weather.
Mahaweli Authority planned to drain Bowathenna Reservoir for sediment study and removal.
Parliament approved a supplementary estimate for Yala paddy purchases.
Officials were directed to develop safe fruit-ripening certification and pilot facilities.
Eligible rice millers and cooperatives may receive interest-free loans up to Rs. 25 million.
The Yala paddy harvest purchasing programme began on August 12.
Sri Lanka and ADB signed a $200 million policy-based loan agreement for trade, investment and industry.
Cabinet approved a monthly allowance of LKR 5,000 for 5,530 eligible students.
Cabinet authorised drafting legislation to establish the Sri Lanka Education Council.
A joint ministry training programme launched to strengthen community health emergency preparedness.
The revised total estimated cost for Sethsiripaya Stage III is LKR 38.48 billion.
Cabinet approved a revised LKR 25.58 billion agreement with Maga Engineering for Sethsiripaya Stage III.
The article describes an information management system for the Kandy Esala Perahera.
Alumni-funded smart microgrid was installed and inaugurated at Peradeniya Engineering Faculty.
President proposed combining military research centres into a national centre.
August Aswesuma benefits for both phases were scheduled for bank transfer on August 19.
Officials said steps were underway to appoint an audit team for ten divisional secretariats.
Coral planting programmes were completed off Unawatuna and Seenigama under a coastal restoration project.
Government allocated capital grants for over 100 local authority revenue projects.
Ceremonies launched over 100 local authority revenue-generating projects.
Audit reported phase two expenditure on the e-Grama Niladhari project.
Police paid annual rent for 325 buildings in 2025.
Applications opened for eight paramedical training courses for 2026.
Central Bank held a Jaffna digital payments promotion event on August 7 and 8.
People’s Bank made a contribution to the Kandy Esala Perahera.
About LKR 11 billion was allocated for development work at Badulla Teaching Hospital.
Officials discussed a repayable loan scheme for small mills buying paddy at a minimum price.
Cabinet approved awarding the contract to build three fuel storage tanks at Muthurajawela.
Cabinet approved financing for the Northern and Eastern integrated regional development programme.
Cabinet approved equity capital for Metro Transit operations and infrastructure development.
Cabinet approved converting 30,000 metric tonnes of government paddy stocks into rice for market release.
Battery storage systems at 16 transmission substations reached the final construction stage.
Health Ministry handed over a mobile laboratory bus to the National Transport Medical Institute.
Applications opened for eight paramedical training courses.
District officials said a committee would develop lasting solutions to flooding.
President directed officials to provide facilities for relocating the Government Analyst Department.
Cabinet approved procuring 50 additional low-floor buses through a repeat order.
Yala-season fertiliser assistance was credited to Galle farmers’ bank accounts.
The Ganethenna–Kadugannawa road section reopened after a temporary weather-related closure.
Parliamentary committee reviewed a Rs. 71.7 billion relief package funded through existing budget reallocations.
The package reallocated Rs. 52.8 billion for fuel-related relief payments and budget replenishment.
The package allocated Rs. 15 billion for the Ceylon Electricity Board.
The package allocated Rs. 8.2 billion for the Aswesuma programme.
A parliamentary committee approved a pilot study of proposed Aswesuma eligibility criteria.
Rs. 6.793 billion was scheduled for rural small-bridge development during 2026–2029.
Bridge projects funded by the 2026 allocation had reached 29% progress.
